title: Phase transitions in non-Hermitian spherical integrals
abstract: We study the large-$N$ asymptotics of a constrained spherical integral for non-Hermitian random matrices, in which the norms and mutual scalar product of two vectors are fixed. In the delocalized regime, the asymptotics are governed by the non-Hermitian transforms $\mathcal R_1$ and $\mathcal R_2$. At saddle-point level, the constrained integral exhibits a transition to a localized regime controlled by the largest singular value of a shifted matrix and by the overlap of its associated left and right singular vectors. Motivated by the Hermitian spherical-integral mechanism and by the Coulomb-gas picture, we formulate conjectures for one-eigenvalue large deviations and boundary fluctuations. Throughout, our analysis is carried out in the spirit of mathematical physics.
summary: This paper analyzes the asymptotic behavior of constrained spherical integrals for non-Hermitian random matrices. It identifies a critical phase transition point determined by the largest singular value of a related matrix. The work develops conjectures for large deviations, extending established techniques from Hermitian random matrix theory to the non-Hermitian setting.
main_problem: The paper studies the large-N asymptotics of constrained spherical integrals for non-Hermitian random matrices, focusing on identifying phase transitions between delocalized and localized regimes.
main_result: The constrained integral exhibits a transition governed by the largest singular value of a shifted matrix, leading to conjectures for one-eigenvalue large deviations and boundary fluctuations.
method: The analysis employs saddle-point methods, extending techniques from Hermitian random matrices (like the Coulomb-gas picture) to the non-Hermitian setting using complex analysis and singular value decomposition.
model_or_system: The model involves non-Hermitian random matrices and a constrained spherical integral $H_{q,N}(\alpha,  eta)$ defined by fixing norms and mutual scalar products of associated vectors.
key_observables: The constrained integral $H_q$, the largest singular value $\sigma_{\max}(z)$, and the one-particle rate function $\Psi_V(z)$.
important_parameters: The parameters $\alpha$ and $ eta$ defining the constraints, and the spectral density $ho_\mu(z)$ of the limiting measure $\mu$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the empirical spectral measure converges to a deterministic measure $\mu$ with compact support, and relies on the validity of the large-N limit and saddle-point approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the mean real part of the overlap $\langle u_1, v_1 angle$ with the mean top singular value $\Sigma(q)$ for the Ginibre ensemble.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by comparing to Hermitian cases, develops the saddle-point analysis for the non-Hermitian integral, identifies the transition point based on singular values, and concludes with conjectures for large deviations.
why_interesting: The mathematical framework of analyzing phase transitions in random matrix integrals, especially the transition from delocalized to localized regimes, has deep parallels with localization phenomena studied in disordered systems and quantum many-body physics.
